findings.summary: The one-related-stem floor, matched against all criteria together with a 3-letter shared prefix, will likely accept realistic omissions that have no path or file token. No corpus case pins this as a known gap.
findings.evidence: I traced the rule by hand on this job's own request and reading (not run). Drop criterion 1, so the main refusal behaviour is missing, and keep criteria 2-8. Bullet 1's specific stems include 'show' (from 'shows'), because bullet 2 and the request paragraph do not use that word. Criterion 2 ('A test shows a request that allows a split ...') contains 'shows', so bullet 1 counts as covered. Under related(), any 4-letter stem also matches by a 3-letter prefix ('show' and 'should', 'pas' and 'past'). Every planned Refuse case is a contrived near-identical pair or a path/file-token pair. The verbatim fzx0 case is caught only because bullet 2 contains CHANGELOG.md. Fix: Add a corpus case: this job's request verbatim, and this job's reading criteria 2-8 with criterion 1 removed. If the check accepts it, tag it as a known gap (like `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today`) and name the limit in the doc. Consider also dropping very common verbs (show, test, pass, run, check) from specific stems when other bullets don't remove them. The replay can judge whether that tightening stays under the 15% limit.
findings.location: Decision 1 / is_covered rule; Demonstration for criterion 3 (corpus cases)

findings.summary: "You can't split this job" would count as permission to split, because apostrophes become spaces before the 'n't' check.
findings.evidence: Step 1 turns punctuation into spaces and matches whole words. "can't" becomes "can t": the permission word 'can' is present and neither 'not' nor 'n't' is, so the sentence passes as affirmative. The same holds for "couldn't". The criterion-2 demonstration has no contraction case. Fix: Check for negation before replacing punctuation (look for an "n't" suffix or a list of contracted forms such as can't, couldn't, mustn't, shouldn't), and add a "You can't split this job." -> Err case to the criterion-2 test.

findings.summary: The plan doesn't say where coverage.rs goes in the two source lists. Their order matters to the source-text tests.
findings.evidence: refusal_corpus.rs:2668-2669: 'The child modules come first, so a search for a function finds it before any test text that names it.' The criterion-8 test splits on `pub fn check_request_coverage(`. If coverage.rs came after reading.rs, a test string that contains that text could be found first. Fix: In both lists, insert `include_str!("reading/coverage.rs")` (and the `../src/` form) before the line for reading.rs, for example after replay.rs.

findings.summary: The doc-link assertion searches all text before `pub fn check_reading_acceptance(`, not just that function's doc block.
findings.evidence: Any earlier text in the joined source that holds [`check_request_coverage`] would satisfy the test, even if the link were missing from the doc of `check_reading_acceptance`. Fix: Assert on the `///` block directly above `pub fn check_reading_acceptance(` (from the last non-doc line before it).

summary: Verdict: accept, with three minor findings and one nit. The plan matches the request and the reading. The new check `check_request_coverage` is added as the last `step!` line in `refusing_check`. I confirmed that `check_reading_references` is the last step today (checks.rs:546) and that the corpus anchor test inserts before that line (refusal_corpus.rs:2752). The helpers the plan reuses exist with the stated visibility: `is_bullet` (topics.rs:266), `request_words` (outcome.rs:141), and `declared_percent`/`normalised` (replay.rs:216-227). The replay limit is declared + 5 points (replay.rs:161, 304-308), and the replay reads the declared share from the reading's criteria (replay.rs:263-290). `governed_reading` exists (reading.rs:4527). `INPUT_FORMS` has 52 entries (refusal_corpus.rs:90). The exemptions for readings that decline or ask a question follow the pattern of the sibling checks (outcome.rs:315, terms.rs:273). The demonstrations use real entry points with no doubles, and each would fail without the behavior. The dependents list covers the readers I found by grep. The minor findings: the one-stem coverage floor is so lenient that realistic omissions without a path or file token may pass, and no corpus case pins that as a known gap; the allow-split negation list misses "can't" after apostrophes are turned into spaces; and the plan doesn't say where coverage.rs goes in the two `reading_source()` lists. None of these blocks a criterion.
